title: Shared Struct Fields with Inconsistent Meanings (Dog Tag Fields)
damaged_code:
```rust
struct Order {
    id: u64,
    is_vendor_order: bool,
    destination_or_supplier: String, // Shipping address if false, vendor name if true
}
```
pattern: Using a single struct field to store different domain meanings based on the state of a flag in another field.
why_bad: It breaks type safety, hides business rules, and couples unrelated customer-shipment and supplier-order tracking logics together, leading to silent state corruption.
detection: A single string/raw field whose documentation or conditional branches indicate it holds distinct conceptual types based on a boolean flag.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2nd Edition), Chapter 12: "dog tag fields", p. 326-327.
